headline: Methods tackle ambient RNA, cross-species integration and spatial gene programs
label: Single Cell Transcriptomics Methods
summary: Recent preprints and publications extend single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analysis to ambient RNA, reference choice, and analysis stability testing.
synthesis: The common thread is methodological: how analytic choices in transcriptomic workflows shape biological conclusions, and how new frameworks address those sensitivities. Several items target reproducibility and reliability. Truecell reimplements Seurat's deterministic single-cell outputs in Python, broadSeq benchmarks differential expression methods on mouse organ and human cancer data, and scStable injects bulk-derived between-sample variation to test analysis stability. Others address specific confounders: AmbiDose removes ambient RNA per cell, reducing cross-species UMIs by 92% while retaining 99.6%; a protein language model maps one-to-one gene homologs for cross-species integration; and reference genome choice alters breast cancer RNA-seq quantification. Spatial and isoform-level methods (DeSPA, SORT, IsoGraph) extend gene program inference, and DKO reports rising cross-cell heterogeneity of virtual perturbation responses with aging. The thread is dominant rather than uniform, as the set also spans metabolomics, circadian analysis and ncRNA testing.
